en.name: Sesame seeds
en.summary: Sesame seeds keep 5 years in a sealed container in a cool, dry, dark cupboard — one of the longest figures in the whole store cupboard. That is a flavour and usability window, not a safety deadline, and the seed's tiny, tough coat is what makes it possible.
en.pantry: 5 years in an airtight jar, cool, dark and dry. It is a striking number for an oily seed, and the reason is scale: each seed is small, whole and tightly hulled or coated, so very little oil is exposed to air at any one time. Nothing grows in a dry seed, so what you are protecting is the flavour, and the way to protect it is to keep the jar sealed, out of the sun and away from the hob. Toasted sesame seeds are a different matter and lose their aroma far faster — toast only what a dish needs.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for sesame seeds, and with a 5-year cupboard figure there is little reason to give up the space. Cold does no harm, and for a large bag in a hot, humid kitchen it is a reasonable precaution against both rancidity and pantry moths. Use a properly airtight jar and let it warm before opening so condensation does not clump the seeds.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published either. Sesame seeds hold almost no water, so freezing does nothing to them, but it also earns very little when the cupboard already runs for years. Ground sesame and sesame paste are a different product with a much shorter life, and those genuinely do benefit from cold.
en.thawing: Nothing to thaw. Let any chilled or frozen jar come back to room temperature sealed before opening it.
spoilage: A bitter or sharp taste when you chew a pinch — the oil has turned.
A smell of old cooking oil rather than a faint, sweet nuttiness.
Seeds clumped together, meaning moisture has got into the jar.
Mould, webbing or moths in a jar stored somewhere damp.
tips: Taste a pinch raw before using seeds from an old jar; bitterness carries into the dish.
Toast in a dry pan just before use, and only as much as you need.
Keep black and white seeds in separate labelled jars; they look alike once mixed.
Write the purchase date on the jar — five years is longer than anyone remembers.

faq.q: How long do sesame seeds keep?
faq.a: 5 years in a sealed jar in a cool, dry, dark cupboard.

faq.q: Do sesame seeds need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: No refrigerated timeline is published and the cupboard figure is already very long. Cold is a reasonable precaution for a large bag in a hot kitchen, nothing more.

faq.q: How can you tell if sesame seeds have gone bad?
faq.a: Chew a few. Rancid sesame is bitter and tastes of old oil, and that bitterness carries straight into whatever you sprinkle it on.

zh.name: 芝麻
zh.summary: 芝麻密封放在陰涼、乾燥、避光的櫥櫃可放 5 年，是整個乾貨櫃裡最長的數字之一。那是風味與可用性的窗口，不是安全的死線；能做到這件事，靠的是那層又小又韌的種皮。
zh.pantry: 氣密罐、陰涼、避光、乾燥，5 年。對一個含油的種子來說，這是很驚人的數字，原因在於尺度：每一粒都小、完整、皮又緊，任何時刻暴露在空氣中的油都非常少。乾燥的種子長不出東西，所以你要保護的是香氣，方法就是罐子密封、避免日曬、遠離爐台。炒過的芝麻是另一回事，香氣散得快得多——需要多少才炒多少。
zh.fridge: 芝麻沒有公布的冷藏期限，而櫥櫃既然給到 5 年，實在沒什麼理由讓出冰箱的位子。冷藏不會有害；在又熱又濕的廚房裡，大袋芝麻冰起來，對油耗和穀蛾都算合理的預防。請用真正氣密的罐子，並且回溫後再打開，免得結露讓芝麻結塊。
zh.freezer: 冷凍同樣沒有期限數據。芝麻幾乎不含水，冷凍對它沒有什麼影響，但既然櫥櫃本來就以年計，它也賺不到什麼。磨碎的芝麻與芝麻醬是完全不同的產品，壽命短得多，那些才是真的受惠於低溫的東西。
zh.thawing: 沒有東西要解凍。冰過或凍過的罐子請維持密封回到室溫再打開。
spoilage: 抓一撮嚼一嚼，嚐起來發苦或尖銳——油脂已經走味。
聞起來像久放的食用油，而不是淡淡的甜香。
芝麻黏成一團，代表罐子裡進了水氣。
存放在潮濕處的罐子出現霉、絲網或穀蛾。
tips: 舊罐子的芝麻，用之前先生嚐一撮；苦味會跟著進到菜裡。
要用之前才下乾鍋炒香，而且只炒需要的量。
黑白芝麻分罐標示；混在一起就分不出來了。
在罐上寫購買日期——五年比誰的記性都長。

faq.a: 密封放陰涼、乾燥、避光的櫥櫃，5 年。
沒有公布冷藏期限，而櫥櫃的數字本來就很長。熱廚房裡的大袋芝麻冰起來算是合理的預防，僅此而已。
嚼幾粒。油耗的芝麻會苦、有久放的油味，而且那個苦味會原封不動進到你撒它的任何東西裡。
